reasoning: The package is a standard binary distribution that downloads pinned, checksummed artifacts from the official upstream domain. The PKGBUILD contains no dangerous top-level execution or obfuscated code. The disagreement was solely due to transient API errors in one model preventing it from reviewing trivial metadata files (.gitignore, .SRCINFO), which were successfully reviewed and cleared by another model.
disagreement_analysis: The qwen3 model encountered HTTP 400 errors when auditing .gitignore and .SRCINFO, resulting in an 'inconclusive' overall verdict. The deepseek model successfully audited all files and found them safe. The openrouter report is marked as advisory and does not count as a vote.
coverage_issues: qwen3 model failed to review .gitignore and .SRCINFO due to LLM API errors (HTTP 400).
learnings: Transient API errors on trivial metadata files (like .gitignore and .SRCINFO) should not force an 'inconclusive' security verdict if the core executable files (PKGBUILD) were successfully audited and found safe. The tool should handle partial audit failures gracefully and base the verdict on the successfully reviewed security-critical files.
